info.syllabusName: Culture of English-Speaking Countries_Văn hóa các nước nói tiếng Anh
info.timeAllocation: Study hour (150h) = 45 contact hours (60 sessions) + 1 hour final exam + 104 hours self-study
info.description:
* This course is designed to introduce students to significant features of cultural, social, political, and artistic life in modern Britain and different aspects of American cultural and socio-political life such as the American Dream & American identity, race, immigration, religion, and the global transmission of American culture. Students will develop a broader and deeper understanding of various aspects of British and American culture.
* The course integrates a range of scholarly texts and up-to-date multimedia materials, allowing students to engage critically with key theoretical concepts and their contemporary evolutions in current events.
* Learning takes place through active class participation, independent study, project-based assignments, group presentations, debates, and creative multimedia tasks (including responsible use of AI tools).
* Through this course, students will develop academic reading and writing skills, analytical thinking, cultural awareness, teamwork, and oral communication.

Assessment structure:
1) Ongoing assessment
- Assignments: 04*15%: 60% (Lecturers wishing to apply PBL may also combine 2 or 3 assignments into 1 project and adjust the weight accordingly)
- Group Project Essay: 01*20%: 20%
2) Final Examination (FE) 20%
3) Final Result 100%
4) Completion Criteria: Ongoing assessment >0 & Group Project Essay >=4/10, Final Exam Score >=4/10, Final Result >=5/10.
info.studentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination
- Actively participate in class activities
- Fulfil tasks given by instructor before and after class
- Use their own laptop in class only for learning purposes

clos.loDetails: Develop a broader and deeper understanding of key aspects of American historical and cultural developments
Develop a broader and deeper understanding of various aspects of social and cultural context in contemporary Britain
Identify and describe major concepts related to national identity, race relations, immigration, gender politics, and cultural transmission in American and British societies
Produce clear, coherent, and well-structured academic essays and oral presentations on a range of topics in English
Critically appraise a range of materials and integrate additional academic sources to produce informed, evidence-based, and properly referenced analyses
Apply a range of digital technology tools, including multimedia platforms and AI applications, effectively, critically, and responsibly to support learning
Develop and refine collaborative working skills by working effectively in groups to plan, research, create, and deliver assignments
Show autonomy and active engagement by participating constructively in class and taking responsibility for personal learning
Demonstrate openness, respect, and cultural sensitivity when discussing complex topics such as race, immigration, gender, religion, and national identity

sessions.topic:
The transmission of American culture - Suggested activities:
- Using your local environment as a resource, go out with a digital camera and record how the cultural landscape has been American­ised. Examine leisure, retail, fast food outlets, supermarkets, bill­boards and fashion.
- Take an American product or brand and design an advertising campaign for the Vietnamese market. You can present your ideas in a mind map, drawing, or poster. You need to come up with a slogan that appeals to Vietnamese customers (AI application possible).

assessments.knowledgeSkill: Knowledge of studied topics and additional research
assessments.gradingGuide:
In groups of 3, students write an analytical essay on a specific question given by lecturer based on a contemporary source document (newspaper articles, educational videos, news reports, Ted Talks, etc.) related to one of the topics discussed in the course. The essay must:
1) Address the question & topic by referring to specific examples from the source material, drawing on knowledge of studied topics, and researching additional sources to support the analysis.
2) Use appropriate references in APA style.
Word count: 500 words
Students submit the essay at the end of the course (the last day). The essay is the source for the final exam.
Students must also submit the presentation slides for the final exam on the last day of the course. Lecturers will forward the slides to the Exam Department for the final exam presentation.
